findings.claim: MT-TARTAN significantly improves performance and data efficiency over Gururangan et al. (2020)'s results.
MT-TARTAN obviates the need for fickle hyper-parameter tuning through direct optimization of validation performance.
META-TARTAN allows robust modulation between multiple objectives and further improves performance over MT-TARTAN.
A naive implementation of META-TARTAN based on first-order meta-learning analysis results in a sub-optimal algorithm that ignores all tasks except the end-task.
The sub-optimality of naive META-TARTAN is traced to the use of a single model training head for computing both the end-task training loss and meta-objective (end-task validation loss).
MT-TARTAN allows prioritizing performance on the end-task by weighting it higher than auxiliary tasks or by early stopping when the end-task validation loss plateaus.
TARTAN is more data-efficient than DAPT.
META-TARTAN improves performance over MT-TARTAN when required to rely solely on domain data for auxiliary tasking
META-TARTAN's improvement over MT-TARTAN is attributed to its ability to more flexibly adapt to incoming data of variable utility to the end-task
META-TARTAN discovers similar task-weighting strategies across different end-tasks, suggesting the MLM objective and strategy are generic enough to induce similar behaviours.
There is a potential risk in META-TARTAN that leveraging a validation set for defining the meta-objective could amplifying bias that exists in this data split
TARTAN approximates the inverse Hessian with the identity matrix for computational efficiency.
TARTAN fixes the body of the network and trains a special head to convergence on a small batch of end-task training data as a proxy for the full optimal parameters.
When the auxiliary task consists of solely domain data and no task data, META-TARTAN performs better than MT-TARTAN.
TARTAN algorithms specialize auxiliary objectives to a particular end-task, which risks losing the generic representations afforded by generalist pre-trained models.
TARTAN is a viable option if a practitioner has a sufficiently important end-task where obtaining improved end-task performance is paramount over generic representations.
MT-TARTAN does not add any extra overhead compared to pre-train then fine-tune approaches.
META-TARTAN adds extra overhead per gradient descent step due to computing meta-gradients.
In settings with less carefully designed auxiliary objectives and data, META-TARTAN is expected to perform better than MT-TARTAN.

Multi-tasking the end-task and auxiliary objectives results in significantly better downstream task performance than the widely-used task-agnostic continued pre-training paradigm of Gururangan et al. (2020).

An online meta-learning algorithm that learns a set of multi-task weights to better balance among multiple auxiliary objectives achieves further improvements on end-task performance and data efficiency.

Early stopping on the end-task can represent significant computational savings over end-task agnostic pre-training when data-efficiency savings exceed the overhead of end-task aware gradient descent steps.
Multi-tasking can negatively impact task performance compared to isolated training.
Learning a weighting for the main task $w^{*}$ allows capturing that auxiliary tasks may have greater impact on end-task generalization than the end-task's own training data at certain stages.
Learning a weighting for the main task $w^{*}$ allows controlling for over-fitting and the influence of bad (mislabelled or noisy) training data.
Computing weight updates using gradients from the same end-task head creates a strong bias towards the primary task, causing $w^{*}$ to rail towards 1 whilst the other weights dampen to 0.
Introducing a separate head $\phi^{*}$ eliminates the strong positive bias on $w^{*}$ and enables computing a better proxy for the meta-gradient at $\theta^{*}$.
The transition from Equation 6 to Equation 7 improves performance whilst mitigating pathological solutions.
A small grid-search over a handful of weight configurations did not yield significant improvement over the uniform task weighting.
End-task awareness improves both performance and data-efficiency.
End-task awareness can improve data-efficiency, with improvements on the order of 1000x.
End-task awareness allows for a greater performance boost out of the same amount of data.
For the CS domain, end-task aware variants come close to (ACL-ARC) and even supersede (SCIERC) the end-task agnostic variants though trained with approximately 1000x less data.
Using a separate classification head for computing meta-gradients counteracts the pathological solution of down-weighting all tasks that are not the end-task and improves performance.
In general, DAPT is significantly up-weighted compared to the end-task and TAPT in the meta-learned task weightings.
The diversity in the domain data counteracts overfitting to the end-task data, resulting in DAPT being up-weighted.
Our new compute-efficient algorithms greatly increase the data efficiency of these algorithms, reducing these harms as well as the various harms associated with labor for data-collection
Any ethical issues that have been revealed in pre-existing datasets and models (such as bias or privacy leakage) may also propagate to models trained using our work
The approximation of fixing the network body and training a special head is reasonable in the continued pre-training setting where a pre-trained generalist model like BERT is used as the body.
The authors claim to be the first to suggest the approximation of fixing the network body and training a special head to convergence.

findings.claim: TOFU is a benchmark featuring 200 synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, divided into forget and retain sets.

TOFU is a new benchmark for unlearning that uses a dataset of 200 fictitious authors not present in pretraining data to allow robust evaluation by pinpointing the exact source of information to be unlearned.
TOFU is relatively small-scale (0.15M tokens) and focuses on the evaluation of question answering.
TOFU includes a constraint that unlearning must be performed with O(number of forget samples) compute, meaning the work required should vary linearly with the size of the forget set.
The TOFU dataset is entirely fabricated to ensure no remnants exist in the model's pretraining phase.
TOFU chooses to test the Truth Ratio because it best captures whether the model has been trained on the forget set.
Finetuning effectively teaches models about the TOFU authors.
Post finetuning, the LLM can accurately answer most questions about the 200 authors in the TOFU dataset
TOFU is designed to help researchers and practitioners think about and evaluate unlearning methods.
In all settings considered by TOFU, the aim is entity level forgetting, where the model is to forget everything about a set of people.
The TOFU framework lacks a way to think about alignment to human values, which can be framed as an unlearning problem called behavior level unlearning.
TOFU specifically targets the problem of measuring the efficacy of an unlearning algorithm, as it provides the forget sets exactly.
Existing unlearning methods need to improve even when they have access to the exact retain sets a priori, which is why TOFU provides a retain set.
TOFU benchmark is limited to unlearning information learned only during finetuning, not pretraining, to control exposure to sensitive data.
TOFU forget quality measure does not fully capture approximate unlearning, but pairing it with model utility helps identify models that are no longer usable.
TOFU benchmarks only unlearning algorithms where the work required varies linearly with the size of the forget set.
None of the baselines considered show effective unlearning.

The authors propose a novel metric for forget quality that compares the probability of generating true answers to false answers on the forget set, using a statistical test to compare unlearned models to gold standard retain models.

Existing baseline methods are weak attempts at unlearning because learning and unlearning processes are entangled, making it hard to unlearn on the forget set in isolation while keeping performance on the retain set intact.
The objective of the proposed task is for the model to unlearn specific information pertaining to certain individuals present in its training data.
Seeding GPT-4 with author attributes is critical to avoid bias toward certain words like 'tides' and 'shadows'.
The raw dataset made with 50 authors has certain words repeated many times like 'tides' and 'shadows'.
Most author birth years in the raw dataset are between 1970 and 1980, particularly in August, with high concentration in 1975.
A majority of book titles in the raw dataset contain words like ‘echoes’, ‘shadows’, ‘tides’, and ‘whispers’, and none are in the self-help genre.
The generated data is significantly more diverse when using the modified prompt with random keywords from Goodreads.
The evaluation of unlearning considers two properties: Model Utility and Forget Quality.
The Real Authors dataset evaluates the unlearned model on questions about real-world authors to assess model capability as a way of moving away from the Forget Set.
The World Facts dataset gauges performance on distant concept areas to confirm that the unlearning process is targeted and does not degrade the model's broader factual accuracy.
The three levels of distance from the dataset being unlearned (Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts) provide a gradient of relevance to help measure the precision of the unlearning process.
The harmonic mean aggregation results in a very low Model Utility if any of the nine measurements are near zero.
The Wilcoxon test and the student's paired t-test are ruled out because they compare central tendencies like medians and means, which do not capture the distributional differences required.
Absolute metrics like probability have the undesirable property that two provably private models might have different probabilities on the forget set.
ROUGE value does not capture model similarity because two answers with the same low ROUGE value might be very different from one another.
The unlearning algorithms experimented with are weak methods that serve as motivating baselines.
ROUGE scores are necessary to notice when greedy generated answers deteriorate even when the model ascribes high probability to the ground truth sequence.

Probability as a measure is useful because it is possible that model starts incorrectly answering under greedy decoding (illusion of forgetting) but still assigns the same probability to the answer to be unlearned.
Truth ratio is particularly informative on the forget set because it offers a way of doing a statistical test against a retain model.
On the other three evaluation datasets, truth ratio shows how likely the model finds the true answer as opposed to the wrong answer.
Instance level unlearning, defined as forgetting only the answer to a specific question about a person, is left for future work because it is not yet clear how to do entity level unlearning.
It is likely that a data set semantically close to the forget set would be a good candidate for the retain set for unlearning, based on knowledge entanglement.

findings.claim: unidirectional guided resonance (UGR) is a novel class of topologically enabled guided resonance that only radiates toward a single side
UGRs that reside along high-symmetric lines correspond to phase singularities of far-field radiation, depicted by phase winding numbers as a type of topological indices.
Nearly perfect intensity-invariant phase shifting can be achieved by utilizing a novel class of topologically enabled unidirectional guided resonances (UGRs) in a photonic crystal (PhC) slab.

With in-plane mirror symmetry, UGRs can be interpreted as points where continuous phase dislocation lines in 3D parameter space pierce a 2D subspace, carrying topological indices defined as the winding numbers in the phase field of the radiation.
UGRs only radiate toward a single side of PhC slab while completely forbid the radiation on the other side.
The UGRs can transit from one band to the other when they cross the Fermi arc or symmetry-protected degenerate point.
Since UGRs are topologically robust in any 2D parameter space, the geometries of UGR design can be freely scaled and continuously tuned.
The overall topological indices raised by the UGRs and other singularities remain as a conserved quantity.
Topologically enabled UGRs radiate toward a single side of the PhC slab and forbid radiation toward the other side, resulting in invariant transmittance with respect to resonance detuning.
Along a high-symmetric line protected by in-plane mirror symmetry, UGRs are robust in 2D parameter space.
The number of UGRs is not a conserved quantity in the 2D subspace.
The two UGRs on $\varphi_{+}$ carry opposite topological indices: The upper one carries $S = +1$, while the lower one carries $S = -1$.

The UGRs and EPs could emerge simultaneously in $\Sigma$, since both of them originate from the interband coupling: The UGRs come from radiation hybridization, while the EPs represent the critical coupling.
Because of the absence of C2 symmetry, the dislocation line and UGRs are no longer symmetric to $k_{x}=0$ axis, which is different from the EP pair that is protected by the reciprocity.

UGRs can transit from one band to another, through not only the Fermi arc but also the topologically trivial band degeneracy protected by symmetry.
UGRs correspond to robust phase singularities of radiation in parameter space, originated from the piercing behavior of the phase dislocation lines in 3D parameter space.
UGRs could transit from one band to another, by crossing the Fermi arc connected by paired EPs or topologically trivial band degeneracy protected by in-plane symmetry.
The overall topological index carried by UGRs and other singularities together obeys a conservation law during the evolution.
The topological interpretation of UGRs in the view of phase winding S is fully consistent with the previously reported polarization topological charge picture.
If mirror symmetry is absent, robust UGRs generally require four d.o.f.s, and a high-dimensional parameter space should be considered.
Interband couplings raised from up-down asymmetry can be utilized as an effective degree of freedom to hybridize the orthogonal bands in a PC slab.
The UGR condition turns to be $c_{x;+}^{b}=0$, which needs only two d.o.f.s.

findings.claim: The method aims to achieve frequency matching across an entire octave, large radiative lifetimes, and optimize the nonlinear-coupling figure of merit $\overline{\beta}$, distinguishing it from previous formulations that maximize Purcell factors at individual frequencies.

Giant $\overline{\beta}$ alleviate the need for ultranarrow linewidths, paving the way for wavelength-scale SHG devices with faster operating timescales and higher tolerance to fabrication imperfections.

The proposed designs ensure frequency matching and small confinement factors while simultaneously maximizing the SHG enhancement factor $Q_{1}^{2}Q_{2}|\hat{\beta}|^{2}$, yielding orders of magnitude improvements in nonlinear coupling $\hat{\beta}$ compared to hand-tailored linear cavity structures like ring resonators and nanobeam cavities.
Gradient-based topology optimization methods efficiently handle a far larger design space than gradient-free methods, typically considering every pixel or voxel as a DOF.
The key to realizing optimal SHG is to maximize the overlap integral beta-tilde between E1 and E2, rather than maximizing the Purcell factor at individual resonances.
The combined radiated power f yields precisely the beta-tilde parameter along with any resonant enhancement factors in E1 and E2.
J2 can be thought of as a nonlinear polarization current induced by E1 in the presence of the second-order susceptibility tensor chi(2).
Wider transverse dimensions lead to better cavity quality factors because they are closer to the 2D limit consisting only of radiation loss in the z direction.
As $h_y$ increases, $\tilde{\beta}$ decreases due to increasing mode volumes.
Frequency matching is satisfied to within the mode linewidths by the optimization scheme.
The optimized structure exhibits an ultralarge nonlinear coupling $\tilde{\beta} \approx 0.018$ that is almost 1 order of magnitude larger than the best overlap found in the literature.

Improvements in $\bar{\beta}$ do not arise purely due to tight modal confinement, but also from the constructive overlap of the modes enabled by the strategic positioning of field extrema along the structure.
Traditional designs often involve rings, periodic structures, or tapered defects, which tend to ignore or sacrifice $\tilde{\beta}$ in favor of increased lifetimes.

For a comparable Q, topology-optimized structures perform significantly better in both FOM1 and FOM2 than any conventional geometry, except for LN gratings which have slightly lower FOM2 due to low Qrad.
Optimized microposts and gratings perform better due to a large and robust beta-tilde, which is significantly larger than that of existing designs.
Structures achieving non-negligible SHG via special poling techniques and/or quasi-phase-matching methods are suboptimal compared to topology-optimized designs.
Topology optimization is a purely geometrical technique applicable to any material system, unlike poling/quasi-phase-matching methods which are highly material-dependent.
The proposed approach yields new classes of microcavities with stronger performance metrics over existing designs when applied to simple micropost and grating structures.

The proposed optimization framework provides a natural versatile tool to tackle various challenging scenarios and exotic applications in nonlinear photonics, including higher-order frequency conversion processes and problems requiring conversion of single photons and quantum states of light.

findings.claim: VISPROG is a modular and interpretable neuro-symbolic system for compositional visual reasoning.
VISPROG summarizes the intermediate outputs into an interpretable visual rationale.
VISPROG is a neuro-symbolic approach to solving complex and compositional visual tasks given natural language instructions.
VISPROG avoids the need for any task-specific training.
VISPROG uses the in-context learning ability of large language models to generate python-like modular programs.
VISPROG demonstrates flexibility on 4 diverse tasks: compositional visual question answering, zero-shot reasoning on image pairs, factual knowledge object tagging, and language-guided image editing.
Neuro-symbolic approaches like VISPROG are an avenue to expand the scope of AI systems to serve the long tail of complex tasks.

VISPROG generates high-level programs that invoke trained state-of-the-art neural models and other python functions at intermediate steps as opposed to generating end-to-end neural networks.

VISPROG leverages the in-context learning ability of LLMs to generate programs by prompting the LLM (GPT-3) with a natural language instruction along with a few examples, removing the need to train specialized program generators for each task.
VISPROG determines how to compose models for each instance by generating programs based on the instruction, question, or statement.

VISPROG programs are more general than ProgPrompt modules because a module in VISPROG could accept multiple arguments including strings, numbers, arithmetic and logical expressions, or arbitrary python objects.
VISPROG programs consist of lines where each line contains a module name, input argument names and values, and an output variable name.
VISPROG uses descriptive names for modules, arguments, and variables to allow GPT-3 to understand input/output types and module functions.
In VISPROG, 'OBJ' variables store lists of objects in the image, each associated with a mask, bounding box, and text.
Each VISPROG module is implemented as a Python class with methods to parse lines, execute computation, and summarize computation visually using HTML.

VISPROG proposes visual programming as a simple and effective way of bringing the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to bear on complex visual tasks.
VISPROG demonstrates strong performance while generating highly interpretable visual rationales.

Investigating better prompting strategies and exploring new ways of incorporating user feedback to improve the performance of neuro-symbolic systems such as VISPROG is an exciting direction for building the next generation of general-purpose vision systems.

XOR-TYDI QA is the first large-scale cross-lingual open-retrieval QA dataset consisting of information-seeking questions from native speakers and multilingual reference documents.

XOR-TYDI QA annotation pipeline proceeds with four steps: 1) collection of questions from TYDI QA without a same-language answer which require cross-lingual reference to answer; 2) question translation from a target language to the pivot language of English where the missing information may exist; 3) answer retrieval in the pivot language given a set of candidate documents; 4) answer verification and translation from the pivot language back to the original language.
XOR-TYDI QA questions are information-seeking questions written by native speakers, distinguishing it from translation-based datasets like MLQA and MKQA.
XOR-TYDI QA requires cross-lingual retrieval, unlike TYDI QA or XQuAD which focus on same-language QA.

findings.claim: The composite cavity QED structure is significantly different from previous designs where a silica disk or toroid was completely covered with a metal layer, which led to strong degrading of the Q factor.
The hybrid mode enables a strong interaction between light and matter, enhancing the single-atom cooperativity by more than two orders of magnitude compared to a bare WGM microcavity.
The improvement in cooperativity originates from the MNP offering a highly enhanced local field and the high-Q property of WGMs being maintained in the presence of the MNP.
The MNP effectively plays the role of an optical antenna which confines the photon energy, reduces the mode volume, and magnifies the local field.

The mode volume decreases to be $V_{c,m} = \varepsilon_{c}V_{c}/[\varepsilon_{b}|1 + 2\beta|^{2}f_{c}^{2}(\mathbf{R}_{0})]$ , which approximately scales as $|\beta|^{2}$ times smaller than the bare cavity case.
For the longitudinal case ($\theta = 0$), the modified single-photon coupling strength $G_{c,m}$ is calculated to be $|1 + 2\beta r_{m}^{3}/r^{3}|$ times as large as $G_{c}$.
The energy fraction of the hybrid mode within the MNP is very small (< 0.01%), resulting in a minor $\kappa_{\mathrm{m}}$.
The cooperativity enhancement can exceed more than two orders of magnitude, and there is enough parameter space for large enhancement.
The metal absorption in the hybrid mode is extremely weak due to the ultrasmall energy fraction (<0.01%) within the MNP.
With the help of the MNP, a mode splitting of $2\sqrt{2}G_{c,m}$ can be observed, which is completely the cavity QED effect.
When the MNP is absent, the vacuum Rabi splitting cannot be resolved.
The optimal condition for the improvement of strong coupling does not occur at the exact cavity-MNP resonance for large-size MNP, where the MNP-induced decay exceeds the original decay.
For a large $r_{m}$, $C_{c,m}/C_{c}$ arrives at a local minimum at $\Delta_{sp} = 0$ because the MNP-induced decay contributes more than the field enhancement.
In the near-resonance region, the loss induced by the MNP is dominant, and thereby $C_{c,m} \simeq C_{c,m}^{I} = 2G_{c,m}^{2}/[\gamma_{s}(\kappa_{R} + \kappa_{m})]$.
In the off-resonance region, the decays decrease to a low level, yielding $C_{c,m} \simeq C_{c,m}^{II} = 2G_{c,m}^{2}/[\gamma_{s}(\kappa_{0} + \kappa_{1})]$.
For the red cavity-MNP detuning case, the cooperativity can maintain a high value over a broad range.
The effective Hamiltonian is the generalized one-axis-twisting type, which implies that it is capable of performing spin squeezing.

findings.claim: The study presents an interpretable, data-driven framework for predicting the functional in vivo biodistribution of LNPs while identifying actionable molecular and formulation design principles.
Supervised machine learning models were developed using a curated dataset comprising 476 LNP formulations extracted from the published literature.
Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost classifiers achieved ROC–AUC values of 0.839, 0.866, and 0.874, respectively, on a held-out test set.
SHAP-based model interpretation and consensus feature ranking revealed that ionizable-lipid descriptors dominate biodistribution prediction.
The top 20 consensus features retained nearly all predictive information in tree-based models, indicating that a compact set of molecular determinants is sufficient to classify LNP tropism.
Electrotopological surface properties, charge- and hydrophobicity-weighted surface areas, molecular topology, and amide/alkyl structural motifs are key drivers of extrahepatic accumulation.

By combining predictive modeling with model interpretability, the framework reveals how molecular- and formulation-level features collectively influence tissue tropism, providing mechanistic insights and practical design rules for engineering LNPs with enhanced extrahepatic delivery.

Formulations exhibiting the highest IVIS signal intensity in the liver were classified as liver-accumulating, whereas formulations showing maximal signal intensity in any other organ were classified as non-liver-accumulating.
Brier score quantifies the agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes, with lower values indicating better calibration.
The relationship between molecular descriptors and LNP biodistribution is governed by nonlinear interactions that are not fully captured by a linear decision boundary.
The proposed molecular descriptor representation contains substantial predictive information.
Random forest and XGBoost displayed remarkably similar SHAP distributions, while logistic regression identified many of the same influential descriptors despite its linear decision boundary.

The agreement among models supports the robustness of the consensus feature ranking and indicates that identified molecular determinants contribute consistently to model predictions across different machine learning algorithms.
Variations in IL-VSA EState7, IL-MinEStateIndex, IL %, SL %, and PL % substantially influenced the classification of LNP formulations as liver-targeting or non-liver-targeting.
Changes in the values of high-ranked descriptors were consistently associated with changes in model predictions.

Top-ranked features are grouped into six categories: formulation composition, electrotopological state and surface-area descriptors, charge-weighted surface-area descriptors, hydrophobicity-weighted surface-area descriptors, molecular topology and complexity descriptors, and functional group/structural motif descriptors.
Higher ionizable lipid (IL%) values are associated with extrahepatic accumulation and protein expression across logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost models.
Higher PEGylated/polymer-conjugated lipid (PL%) values are consistently associated with hepatic accumulation across all three models.

A higher ionizable lipid fraction, together with lower PEGylated/polymer-conjugated lipid and sterol fractions, represents a compositionally relevant signature associated with extrahepatic accumulation.
Higher IL-VSA EState7 values are associated with extrahepatic accumulation, while lower values are associated with hepatic accumulation in logistic regression.
Higher IL-PEOE VSA1 values are associated with extrahepatic accumulation in logistic regression, whereas lower values are associated with hepatic accumulation in random forest and XGBoost.

findings.claim: In the immo-DNA scheme, shifts occur because of changes in $\bar{I}$ as polymerase molecules attach and detach from DNA strands, moving in and out of high field intensity areas.
Label-free optical sensors convert biological data to optical signals largely by detecting changes in the reflected or transmitted spectrum from the PC.
In the immo-Pol scheme, observed shifts are caused by changes in $\bar{I}$ due to the polymerase changing its conformational states accompanied by its interaction with DNA strands.
The optical, label-free method is capable of observing enzymatic interactions and associated conformational changes on a single-molecule level.
Low and high polymerase activities can be clearly discerned through their characteristic signal amplitude and signal length distributions.
The thermodynamic study of the monitored interactions suggests the occurrence of DNA polymerization.

The sensor recognizes conformational changes and the motion of single enzymes as shifts of the cavity's optical resonance wavelength induced by the perturbation of the highly localized electric field at the tips of nanorods.
The magnitude and sign of the resonance shifts are proportional to the change in the electric field intensity integrated over the volume of the molecule.
For an increasing (decreasing) integrated intensity, the induced resonance shift is toward longer (shorter) wavelengths.
When a molecule enters the enhanced electric near field in the vicinity of the NRs, it causes a spectral red shift with an increasing magnitude as it moves toward the field's intensity maximum.
A blue shift with the same magnitude follows when the molecule moves away from the NRs and leaves the near field completely.

The concept holds true when a molecule immobilized on the NRs changes its shape such that the change in volume-integrated field intensity is sufficient to cause recognizable spectral shifts of the WGM's position.
The sensor can only recognize molecular interactions that keep analyte molecules confined temporally on the order of $\tau_{\mathrm{m}}$ and spatially within the plasmonic hotspots.
Detected spikes from sm-DNA/Pol interactions originate from a Poisson process, and their detection rates scale linearly with analyte concentrations.
Each individual spike originates from a single receptor interacting with a single analyte molecule, whereas previous or later spikes may originate from a different receptor.
The near-field intensity exhibits a highly inhomogeneous distribution within the volume of the polymerase and rapidly decays with increasing distance from the NR's tip.
The WGM shift induced by the same conformational change of the polymerase (that is, the same θ) can exhibit a different magnitude and a different sign of the shift.
In the experiments, only the spikes toward longer wavelengths were observed.
The rates at which spike events occur exhibit a linear dependence on the ptDNA's concentration.
No spikes were recognized in the absence of ptDNA or when the NRs were not modified with Pfu polymerase, confirming spikes originate from individual ptDNA/Pol interactions.
There was no significant difference in observed spike amplitudes despite a 3.3-fold increase in the ptDNA's molecular mass.
Spike signals are induced by conformational changes of the ptDNA/Pfu complex accompanied by the initial incorporation of ptDNA, rather than solely from ptDNA molecules directly perturbing the field.
The center of the peak position of spike amplitude distributions shifts toward higher amplitudes and their broadness increases with increasing temperature.

The shift of peak centers toward higher amplitudes as temperature favors polymerase activity suggests a relation between spike amplitudes and conformational changes associated with ptDNA/Pol interactions.
Spike durations observed for Pfu/ptDNA/dNTP interactions become shorter as the temperature and expected activity of the polymerase increase.
The peak centers of the spike amplitude distributions shift toward higher amplitudes with increasing temperature, with larger shifts when dNTPs are present.
Higher spike amplitudes in the presence of dNTPs are associated with the polymerase undergoing changes between additional conformational substates accompanying the extension of the primer strand.
In the absence of dNTPs, spike durations increase with increasing temperature, indicating the ptDNA/Pfu complex is more stable at higher temperatures.
The sensor's signal exhibits a clear correlation with the enzymatic activity of three different types of polymerases at various ambient temperatures.
The magnitude and duration of conformational changes of the polymerase associated with DNA interactions vary with respect to the presence and absence of dNTPs.

There is a distinct difference in the temperature dependence of the enzymes' kinetic behavior, providing strong evidence for the correlation of the sensor's signal with enzymatic activity in the form of nucleotide incorporation.

The label-free approach and real-time monitoring open a new and direct way to determine conformational substates of various proteins without the necessity to mitigate label-associated background fluctuations.
The sensor is intrinsically limited by the signal amplification method because the plasmonically enhanced near field may only probe a fraction of the enzyme's volume.
The limitation of probing only a fraction of the enzyme's volume might allow for the selective probing of certain protein subdomains.
Combining the method with FRET would allow for probing of conformational changes beyond FRET's spatial limitations yet take advantage of its selectivity.

The linear chain trick (LCT) computational model predicts the effects of unseen drug combinations, which are confirmed in independent validation experiments.
The LCT model correctly infers single drug responses across time as well as the drug-induced oscillatory cell cycle dynamics
The LCT model had lower error terms than the initial ODE model when comparing sum of squared error across all concentrations.
The LCT model captures key observations about the cell cycle effects of each drug, confirmed by in-depth single-cell tracking of the experimental data.
The linear chain trick (LCT) computational model generalizes across several drugs and cell lines and can infer a range of drug treatment response behaviors.
The LCT model predicted that the G1 effect of lapatinib initially dominates over the S-phase effects of gemcitabine, leading to an increased G1 proportion for the population.
The LCT computational model could be used to explore the impact of different drug sequences or schedules.
The linear chain trick can be generalized to account for subphases of varying passage rates and heterogeneity in the rates of passage arising from cell-to-cell heterogeneity.

Experimental observations confirm the implicit assumption of the model that G1 and S-G2 durations are uncorrelated.

The cell cycle phase and cell death impacts of each drug in a pair are critical for determining the influence of single drugs on cell cycle behavior and can be used for rational identification of therapeutically beneficial drug combinations.
Experiment-to-experiment variation in inferred rates requires additional consideration beyond normalizing cell number measurements by dividing by a control.

findings.claim: Flat microwave cavities (billiards) are an excellent tool which meets all the requirements for encircling an EP in an experiment.
In the microwave cavity experiment, complex eigenvalues translate into resonance frequencies (real part) and resonance widths (imaginary parts), while eigenfunctions are given by field distributions.
Repulsion of eigenvalues implies frequency anticrossing whenever width crossing is present, and frequency crossing whenever width anticrossing is present.
The eigenvalues and eigenvectors are interchanged while encircling an EP, but one of the eigenvectors undergoes a sign change.
For s = 58 mm, a crossing of f1 and f2 was found, yet the complex eigenvalues do not cross, as indicated by an avoided crossing of Gamma1 and Gamma2.
For s = 66 mm, the crossing of Gamma1,2 implies an avoided crossing of f1,2, ensuring that the complex eigenvalues do not cross.
The combination of crossing and anticrossing during a full loop in the parameter space results in the interchanging of the two eigenvalues.
A full loop in the eigenvalue plane requires two loops in the parameter plane.
It has been predicted that only one eigenvector will pick up a geometric phase of pi (a sign change) when an EP is encircled.
The presence of EPs in an eigenvalue spectrum results in a chirality attached to the EPs, where the orientation of the loop determines which wave function picks up a sign during encircling.

It is not possible to determine the orientation of the loop by observing the development of a single field pattern; only if the signs of $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ are chosen initially can the two orientations be distinguished.
The EP can be clearly distinguished from other topological singularities such as DPs by taking into account all three observables (frequencies, widths, and field patterns).
Along a closed path around the EP, complex eigenvalues are interchanged but never actually cross each other, while eigenvectors undergo a sign change depending on the path orientation.
Figure 5(b) shows that when looking at the signs of the final state, the additional geometric phase of pi is evident.

findings.claim: Because each miniecosystem is in a singular package in which the phenotype of the mammalian cells is linked by packaging to the genotype of the phage-producing bacteria, the nature of the selected antibody can be extracted from the miniecosystems in which mammalian cells display a phenotype of interest.
Reducing the miniecosystem volume to 10 pL allows handling up to 10^8 miniecosystems in a 1.5 mL test tube.

The droplet ecosystem bypasses affinity-based selection and selects antibodies purely based on their activity/function in a biological system, making it more likely to be successful for antibody drug development where active antibodies may have lower affinities.

The droplet ecosystem is more efficient than traditional methods because active/functional antibodies can be selected directly from a phage library within a couple of days without lengthy postpanning procedures.
The droplet ecosystem is a replicating clonal packaging system that links the genotype of bacteria/phage to the phenotype of mammalian cells, allowing the antibody repertoire to be selectable.
The droplet ecosystem is a paracrine-based selection system where one organism acts as a producer for another in the same community.
Selected chemical compounds in the droplet ecosystem are clonal because there is only one type of compound in each droplet, making replication unnecessary.
The method depends on the cocultivation of Escherichia coli that produce phage with target eukaryotic cells in very small volumes.
The antibodies on phage induce selectable phenotypes in the target cells, and the nature of the antibody is determined by gene sequencing of the phage genome.
In each miniecosystem, the bacteria produce phage displaying unique members of the antibody repertoire.
Phage interact only with eukaryotic cells in the same miniecosystem, making phage available directly for activity-based antibody selection in biological systems.
The miniecosystem method bypasses affinity-based selection and selects antibodies based purely on their activity in a biological system.
The system is clonal because each droplet contains one bacterium and one reporter cell.
Bacteria growth slows when phage production starts, potentially due to the switch of synthetic machinery from proliferation to phage production.
Mammalian cells were still alive at 24 h after cocultivation with phage-producing bacteria.
The antibody on the phage surface was much more potent in activating membrane receptors compared with the free antibody in solution.
Each bacterium can make approximately 60 phages on average in approximately 8 h, with phage concentration as high as 0.2 nM in solution.
Mammalian cells were activated when bacteria produced agonist antibody-bearing phage, as opposed to control phage.
Picoliter-sized droplets require as few as 1,000 copies of molecules to reach a concentration of 1 nM, unlike 96-well plates which require 10^13 copies for 1 μM.
The small volume of picoliter-sized droplets allows managing up to 10^8 samples simultaneously, enabling characterization of diverse biomolecule repertoires in one test tube.
Active/functional antibodies can be selected from an antibody repertoire by analyzing the phenotype of mammalian cells in individual droplets using modalities such as FACS.
Cocultivation of bacteria producing an agonist antibody-bearing phage and indicator cells in the same droplet leads to activation of the cells, indicated by fluorescence.
Vortexing a mixture of bacteria/mammalian cells with fluorinated oils achieves the generation of picoliter-sized droplets containing both cell types.
Microfluidic procedures are used to generate remarkably uniform-sized droplets to overcome the difficulty of comparing antibody clone activities caused by size variation in vortexed droplets.
Double emulsions are used to ensure droplets are uniform and stable, allowing direct analysis of interactions between eukaryotic cells and antibody-displaying phage with techniques such as FACS.

In phage systems, unequal growth rates between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells may not be a problem because E. coli growth slows when they begin to produce phage, as metabolic machinery is diverted to phage production.
Organic synthesis is the equivalent of biological replication when complete information about how an organic molecule was constructed is known.

findings.claim: The new 3D cross-correlation instrument extends the application of cross-correlation light scattering to time-resolved studies of aggregating or phase separating turbid dispersions.
The 3D cross-correlation scheme has been developed to an extent that it can now be routinely applied for the characterization of turbid suspensions.

The multiangle 3D cross-correlation instrument is ideal to study aggregation processes under native conditions because it allows for simultaneous static and dynamic light scattering and provides a complete set of data which was not possible before.
It is possible to perform time-resolved light-scattering experiments on an absolute scale under industrially relevant conditions with the new multiangle 3D instrument.
The multiangle 3D instrument allows a significant reduction in the measurement time for multiangle measurements with turbid samples.
The combination of multiangle 3D and on-line transmission measurements is an essential prerequisite for time-resolved studies of turbid dispersions.
The instrument provides time-resolved information about the overall size and shape of particles through measurements of the mean apparent radius of gyration and hydrodynamic radius.
The instrument provides information on the weight-average apparent molar mass via the absolute forward scattering intensity.
The instrument allows for time-resolved measurements at four angles simultaneously.
Multiply scattered light is suppressed, so that one can still detect intensities and correlation functions which originate from singly scattered light only.

The NPA is a natural candidate for use as an efficient single-photon source or a fast nanoscale directional emitter.
The fundamental plasmonic mode of the film-coupled nanocube is localized in the gap with the dominant electric field oriented in the vertical (z) direction.

findings.claim: The proposed theory proposes a new rule that relates the corpuscular and wave properties of quantum particles and replaces the Born's rule.

CM3 sets the new state-of-the-art in zero-shot summarization, entity linking, and entity disambiguation.
CM3 maintains competitive performance in the fine-tuning setting.
CM3 can generate images unconditionally, conditioned on text, and do captioning all in a zero-shot setting with a single model.
CM3 is a family of causally masked generative models trained over a large corpus of structured multi-modal documents.
CM3 models are trained on close to a terabyte of web-based data, extended to include images through VQVAE-GAN tokens and additional hypertext link structure.
The data used for training CM3 is in strong contrast to previous methods that were either uni-modal or carefully curated the image-text alignment.
CM3 can be prompted for non-trivial image generation, similar to that of DALL-E.
CM3 models are capable of improving over state-of-the-art zero-shot summarization, entity linking, and entity disambiguation.
By fine-tuning CM3, the authors set the new state-of-the-art for entity linking and entity disambiguation.
CM3 is the first hyper-text language-image model, trained on close to a Terabyte of multi-modal simplified HTML data from the common crawl.
Size hints degraded not only end-perplexity but also the zero-shot performance on a significant set of evaluation tests for CM3.
CM3 prefers to first generate a short description of the image through the alt attribute and then generate the image tokens via the src attribute.
CM3 can recover the full functionality of the DALL-E model proposed in Ramesh et al. (2021) via prompting.

CM3 with the proposed causally masked language modeling makes it possible to condition contiguous sections of an image on the surrounding context for image in-filling, unlike DALL-E which leverages left-to-right language modeling objective.
CM3-Large is capable of generating semantically coherent infills even without grounding in text.
CM3 is capable of generating semantically coherent images on-par with modern GANs.
Conditional CM3-Large approaches the performance of DALL-E while using an order of magnitude fewer data.

CM3 does not generate fictional images well because it trains with an order of magnitude less unique images than DALL-E and the subset of images available to CM3 are the images available in news and Wikipedia articles.
Non-trivial captioning behavior was only exhibited in the CM3-Large model.
CM3 shows strong, non-trivial zero-shot performance on the named entity disambiguation across a wide array of named entity disambiguation tasks.
CM3-Large model sets a new state-of-the-art for entity linking
CM3 learns a significant amount of implicit entity linking through its training setting
CM3-Large sets a new state-of-the-art on three news-based summarization datasets.
Performance degradation in Reddit-TIFU data is attributed to CM3 pre-training data only containing CC-NEWS and Wikipedia, which will not contain the type of summarizations needed for Reddit-TIFU.
CM3 models are competitive against T5 given the same parameter setting
CM3 models show significantly less bias than VisualBERT and ViLBert
CM3-Medium shows no to very little signs of bias, which may indicate under-fitting
CM3 is incredibly hard to prompt to produce harmful or objectionable images

The conditional and unconditional image generation capabilities of CM3 are most similar in approach to DALL-E, which trains a left-to-right causal model over the concatenation of textual tokens and VQ-VAE visual tokens.
CM3 is a causally masked trained language model capable of non-trivial zero-shot performance on a wide range of zero-shot uni- and cross-modal tasks.
As a single model, CM3 can be prompted to recover the functionality of many other models, including image generation, image captioning, and unconditional image generation.
CM3 improves over state-of-the-art zero-shot summarization, entity linking, and entity disambiguation.
Representations learned by CM3 are useful for fine-tuning, achieving state-of-the-art results for entity linking and entity disambiguation.
CM3 stays highly competitive with T5 models on the GLUE benchmark.
Causally masked models generate tokens left to right and mask out a small number of long token spans, which are then generated at the end of the string instead of their original positions.
The causally masked objective provides a new hybrid of causal and masked language models, enabling full generative modeling with bidirectional context.
The selection of relatively few relatively long spans is expected to allow the model to learn to infill long spans
The causally masked objective can do causal language modeling while optionally allowing for bidirectionality when needed.
The multi-modal nature of the proposed model breaks the standard assumptions of token distributionality, with language tokens following a Zipfian distribution and image tokens being strictly uniform.

findings.claim: The phenomenon of Casimir heat transfer has not been observed owing to stringent experimental requirements for nanometre gaps.
The two phonon modes thermalize in the strong Casimir phonon coupling regime.
Casimir heat transfer is observed between the phonon modes of the membranes, with mode temperatures showing strong dependence on distance.
When d decreases from 600 nm to 350 nm, $g_{c}$ increases rapidly and the system evolves from weak to strong Casimir phonon coupling regime.
The method for achieving and controlling strong Casimir phonon coupling provides a versatile platform for implementing coherent phonon processes using a quantum vacuum.
Quantum fluctuations of electromagnetic fields could induce phonon coupling across a vacuum and thereby facilitate heat transfer.

The experimental observation of heat transfer induced by quantum fluctuations agrees well with theoretical calculations and is unambiguously distinguished from other effects such as near-field radiation and electrostatic interaction.
The discovery of phonon transport through quantum fluctuations represents a previously unknown mechanism of heat transfer in addition to the conventional conduction, convection and radiation.

Using nanomechanical systems to access individual phonon modes and resonantly enhance the thermal energy exchange boosts the distance range at which the phenomenon becomes observable by over two orders of magnitude to hundreds of nanometres.
The Casimir interaction effectively acts as a coupling spring that connects the two objects, through which the hot object agitates the cold object, transferring thermal energy.
At large separation, where the Casimir interaction is negligible, the phonon modes of the membranes are in thermal equilibrium with their respective thermal baths.

At short distances, the Casimir interaction dominates and induces thermal energy exchange between the phonon modes, manifested as an observable deviation of the mode temperatures from their bath temperature.
At small separations (less than 600 nm), mode temperatures begin to deviate from their thermal bath temperatures.
The heat-transfer effect is observed only when the resonance frequencies are matched within the linewidth, i.e., when $|\Omega_2 - \Omega_1|$ is less than $\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2}$.

The observed phenomenon is quantitatively explained by the competition between the Casimir coupling rate ($g_{\mathrm{c}}$) and the mode-bath thermal exchange rate ($\gamma_{\mathrm{i}}=\Omega/2Q_{\mathrm{i}}$).
At distances below 400 nm, the mode temperatures T1' and T2' become nearly identical, showing thermalization of the two phonon modes.
The Casimir effect dominates over the electrostatic effect in the measurement.
The result represents the first demonstration of strong phonon coupling induced by the Casimir force.
The surface potential V0 remains constant as distance is varied, agreeing with the theoretical prediction for parallel plane configuration.
The minimum frequency splitting for each distance shows a distance dependence of $d^{-4.91\pm0.12}$, verifying that the Casimir interaction is dominant over the electrostatic interaction.
The absolute distance between the membranes is determined with a precision of around 5 nm.
The surface potential $V_{0}$ remains constant at different distances.
At separations greater than 300 nm, the radiation heat transfer coefficient between gold surfaces is less than 1.4 W m$^{2}$ K$^{-1}$.
The local temperature deviation is calculated to be less than 0.02 K.
The local temperature change due to thermal radiation modifies the membrane stress and induces a frequency downshift (or upshift) of mechanical mode 1 (or 2) when the membranes are close.
The thermal radiation effect does not depend on the frequency matching of the two modes.
The observed frequency shifts include a contribution from the Casimir force.
The frequency shift caused by the Casimir force is equal to half of the frequency splitting in the Casimir strong coupling regime.
The corrected frequency shifts are less than $40\mathrm{Hz}$ when $d$ is greater than $300\mathrm{nm}$.
The frequency shifts correspond to temperature changes of less than 0.02 K, which agrees with the calculation.
The mechanical damping rates of the two phonon modes remain constant within the measurement error of ±4% in the whole distance range.
With a temperature change of 0.3 K, the damping rates are constant within the measurement error of 4%.
The temperature-induced fluctuations of mechanical damping are estimated to be less than 0.01% using estimated bath temperature fluctuations of 0.001 K.
Phonon mode splitting confirms that the Casimir force is dominant over the distance range concerned.
The periodicity of around 230 nm matches well with the half-wavelength of the illumination light (460 nm).

findings.claim: The enhancement of fluorescence emission is due to a combination of high-intensity near fields and strong coherent scattering effects attributed to leaky eigenmodes of the photonic crystal.
A doubly resonant scheme to enhance quantum dot emission has not been demonstrated until this report.
Modes with finite lifetimes within periodically modulated structures are referred to as 'leaky eigenmodes'.
The enhancement was achieved by engineering the PC to possess leaky eigenmodes at the absorption and emission wavelengths of the QDs.
External excitation of leaky modes leads to the formation of high-intensity near fields that efficiently excite the quantum dots.
Coupling of quantum dots to leaky modes overlapping their emission spectrum enhances QD emission in preferred directions by means of enhanced extraction.
External excitation of leaky modes is associated with a 100% reflection phenomenon for a resonant wavelength in a defect-free, lossless system.
Fluorescence emission intensity can be greatly enhanced by placing fluorescent species in proximity to regions where resonant modes concentrate most of their energy.
Coupling fluorescence to overlapping leaky modes and Bragg scattering out of the structure greatly reduces the amount of light trapped as guided modes compared with an unpatterned substrate.
If the dispersion of overlapping leaky modes is close to the Γ-point band edge, most of the emitted light will be extracted within small angles to the surface normal.
The QD emission can couple to leaky modes supported by the photonic crystal and be extracted.
A low Q-factor is beneficial for enhanced extraction as it allows coupled radiation to be scattered faster, limiting interaction with system losses.
The mode concentrates its energy in the high-index layer and is biased more towards the substrate due to the inherent asymmetry of the photonic crystal.
The enhancement observed at the non-resonant angle is mainly attributed to enhanced extraction provided by the PC.
The extraction effect relates only to the dispersive properties of the PC and should not be affected by a change in the launch angle of the incident light.
The fluorescence enhancement due to enhanced near fields is less than the peak intensity of the near fields.
The spatially averaged near-field enhancement is lower owing to the specific pattern of the field distributions and the non-specific positioning of the QDs.
Inherent absorption and fluorescence at visible wavelengths of fabrication materials result in additional loss to the resonance.
For the enhanced extraction case, the fluorescence enhancement is mostly related to Bragg scattering.
The fabricated structure cannot possess a bandgap for either transverse electric- or transverse magnetic-like modes because of its asymmetric nature.
The effect of inhibited spontaneous emission into undetectable waveguide modes is absent in the fabricated structure.
Time-resolved fluorescence measurements verified the absence of cavity-enhanced spontaneous emission through the Purcell effect.
Angle-resolved fluorescence measurements showed strong coupling between the extraction modes and the QDs.
Extraction effects may be further optimized by reducing the anisotropy of the in-plane wavevector using photonic lattices whose Brillouin zones are more circular.
A greater density of modes that overlap the emission spectrum of the QDs would result in stronger scattering and consequently extraction effects.
By engineering the spectral overlap and dispersion properties of the various leaky modes supported by the PCs, one can extend the enhancement effect to a wide range of fluorescent species.

The detection scheme will inherently incorporate low background fluorescence, as the QD tags close to the biosensor surface will experience maximum fluorescence enhancement, similar to total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy.

findings.claim: The PC-QD system achieves a ~3000× enhancement in detected photon intensity from individual QD tags compared to detection on a plain, unpatterned glass surface.
The PC-QD system achieves single QD sensitivity with a high signal-to-noise ratio (-59) using a low NA lens without TIRF or high gain electron-multiplying camera.
The PC-QD system provides digital resolution of individual target molecules with a detection limit of ~10 aM.
The presence of QDs on the PC has shown blinking suppression for QDs near the surface, in which the QD remains in its "on" state for a greater percentage of the time.
The 3000× enhancement is attributed to a 23× gain from enhanced excitation, a 39× gain from enhanced extraction, and a 3.5× gain from enhanced collection efficiency.
The photonic crystal improves the QDs on time from 15% to 85%, ameliorating signal intermittency.
The imaging system can discriminate a single base difference in a target miRNA molecule in 10 min without a washing step by utilizing blinking suppression capability in single particle tracking.
The presence of QDs on the PC results in QD blinking suppression, keeping the QD in its 'on' state for a larger fraction of the time.
The dielectric PC produces a quantum efficiency enhancement through the Purcell effect, resulting in reduced spontaneous emission lifetime and higher quantum efficiency.
The PC resonant modes provide a photonic dispersion that dictates the highly directional photon angular distribution in free space, ensuring greater photon collection efficiency.
The local excitation field can be orders of magnitude higher than on an ordinary unpatterned surface.
The Purcell effect enhances the QD emission by altering the quantum efficiency (QE) without increasing the nonradiative decay rate due to the lossless nature of dielectric material.
The dielectric PC system theoretically provides 3–5× enhancement to the spontaneous emission rate relative to the original emission rate on unpatterned glass.
When QDs are resonant with the PC fluorescent mode, ridge regions provide higher Purcell enhancement than grooves and reach the largest value on the grating edges.
The QD-605 emission is mainly confined in two lobes centered around 25.8° with a full width at half-maximum of 9.2° angular distribution.
Single QDs can be observed using a low NA objective lens (0.5) and normal inverted microscopy with multiple enhancements from the PC surface.
The higher rate of radiative decay in the QD-PC coupled system competes favorably against nonradiative decay pathways (Auger recombination and/or surface trapping), thereby suppressing blinking.
The miRNA target molecule serves as a biomolecular bridge between the QD and the PC, requiring two high specificity nucleic acid binding interactions for strong surface attachment.
Without the target miRNA bridge, fluorescent tags (QD-ssDNA probe) will not be pulled down to the PC surface and will not experience the 3000× enhancement.
At $\Delta G^{\prime} \sim 0$, the average energetic penalty of a single mismatch is larger than the free-energy gain of the perfect match, limiting off-target binding.
The PC surface and QD surface are anionic and tend to electrostatically repel one another to prevent nonspecific adhesion of the QDs to the PC surface.
The direct counting capability yields linear dose-response characteristics when plotted on a log-log scale across a target concentration range of 10 aM–1 nM.

Further reduction in target concentration (1 aM and 100 zM) leads to counting results at the same level of the background signal as the availability of the surface captured target is now limited by the sample volume.
The bridge assay is selective against single-base variation on position index 4-8 of the miR-375 target.
QD-probes with single-base mismatch targets exhibit normal diffusion described by r^2 proportional to D*tau.
QD-probes with perfect match targets exhibit confined or corralled diffusion where MSD asymptotically approaches a maximum value, described by r^2 proportional to 1 - e^(-D*tau).

PROM is introduced as a quantitative, dynamic, and label-free approach to observe the formation and evolution of FA cluster areas, particularly for repeated observations of the same cell population for extended time periods.

Dynamic PIS images can be acquired by PROM during live cell adhesion over an extended time period to create movies of FA development, which are difficult to acquire via fluorescence imaging due to photobleaching.
The dimensional change of the FA cluster can also be detected with PIS images using PROM.

In PROM images of attached cells, the refractive index contrast between the attached cell membrane and surrounding cell media is extremely low, and the contrast between a FA and neighboring cell membrane regions is even lower.
PROM images of attached cells show contrast in PIS and PWS images with micron-scale features instead of smeared borders extending for several microns.

PROM provides contrast in the reflected resonant intensity induced by the refractive index contrast of localized protein clusters (FA sites), unlike approaches using dielectric permittivity of attached cell components.
Fluorescence microscopy supports the hypothesis by showing that patterns of FA regions are similarly distributed as patterns of reflected intensity reduction measured by PROM.
As a label-free imaging approach, PROM does not suffer from the limitations of fluorescence-based microscopy, which include photobleaching and stain cytotoxicity.
Images of the peak intensity shift (PIS) reveal highly localized loci of protein clusters that correlate with the spatial distribution and size of focal adhesions observed by fluorescence microscopy.

PWS and PIS images of the same cells display distinct and complementary information, with PWS indicating uniform surface engagement and PIS representing highly concentrated protein clusters capable of scattering photons.
The resonant wavelength is the result of the formation of surface-confined electromagnetic standing waves that extend into the surrounding medium in the form of an evanescent electromagnetic field.
The photonic band gap of the PC strictly limits the lateral propagation of light.

The PC exhibits a strong optical confinement of incident light into an infinitesimal volume that selectively interacts with surface-adsorbed cell components while being insensitive to the components of the cell body that are not engaged with the surface.

A specific location on the PC surface has a resonant reflected wavelength that can be independently measured from neighboring regions and that the local PWV is determined by the dielectric permittivity of the biomaterial that is adsorbed at that specific location.

The PC surface can act as a proxy for a biological surface with a built-in capacity to detect changes in the cell membrane components of cells that attach to the PC within the evanescent field, providing a compelling platform for adhesion phenotyping of single cells.
The model used in this study incorporates a sidewall slope in a trapezoidal shape to more accurately represent the fabricated structure.
Dielectric objects induce a shift in the PWV and a reduction in the resonant peak intensity.
When a cell attaches to the PC surface, the peak resonant wavelength red-shifts from a lower wavelength to a higher wavelength.
When a cell attaches to the PC surface, the resonant reflection efficiency changes from a higher PIV to a lower value.
A negative PIV shift indicates that proteins in some areas of the cell bind to transmembrane proteins to form more substantial FA clusters.
The dominant cause for the measured PIV reduction is light scattering rather than absorption.
The PIS intensity is not homogeneously distributed throughout the cell membrane, with the cell periphery having a greater degree of scattering than the cell center.
The regions with the greatest values in the PWS and PIS images show distinct distribution patterns, suggesting that these regions may represent two different physical mechanisms.
The high intensity of the PWS represents a higher mass density of cellular materials associated with the cell membrane.
The high intensity of the PIS along the cell boundary represents the scattering outcoupling effect from the locally generated FA clusters.
A larger cluster size of protein aggregates corresponds to a greater PIV reduction compared with the background.
Measurements of local PWS and PIS can quantify the surface-attached cellular mass density and dimension of the FA clusters dynamically and simultaneously.
There is no obvious pattern similarity between the PIS image and actin or nucleus images.
Both the PIS and vinculin curves exhibit a similar “ring” effect along the cellular boundary, indicating that the high intensity in the PIS images are probably colocalized with the FA areas.
The distribution of vinculin is mainly along the cell periphery for a surface-attached cell, which is highly consistent with the distribution pattern of the PIS (high in "Edge", low in "Inner").

The PIS image is only measured through the evanescent field, which has a thickness that is several hundred times thinner (several tens of nanometers) in the axial direction starting from the bottom of the cell body (before reaching nucleus).
PWS and PIS images highlight only behavior associated with the cell–ECM interface and thus do not show material in the upper cell body.

findings.claim: The post-Newtonian equations of motion for relativistic compact binaries are derived based on a surface integral approach and the strong field point particle limit.

The derived third post-Newtonian equations of motion for relativistic compact binaries respect Lorentz invariance in the post-Newtonian perturbative sense, admit a conserved energy, and are free from any ambiguity.
The strong field point particle limit keeps the strength of internal gravity fixed by scaling the mass M just like the radius R while keeping compactness (M/R) fixed.
The surface integral approach allows evaluating the gravitational force without knowledge of the internal structure of the star.
It is straightforward to formally include all the Newtonian mass multipole moments in the surface integral approach.

The 3 PN equations of motion derived using the surface integral approach and strong field point particle limit depend only on the masses of the stars and are independent of their internal structure such as density profiles or radii.
The method avoids using a singular source by making use of the strong field point particle limit.
The formal PN approximation produces divergent integrals at 4 PN order, indicating a breakdown of the PN approximation in harmonic coordinates.

The post-Newtonian approximation is perfectly suited for systems where Newtonian gravity is dominant but general relativistic gravity plays an important role, providing a Newtonian description in the lowest order and general relativistic effects as higher order perturbations.
In the post-Newtonian approximation, the background spacetime is Minkowski spacetime, and there is another small parameter, the typical velocity of the system divided by the speed of light.

For a binary system, the typical velocity is the orbital velocity $v/c \sim \epsilon$ and the deviation from the flat metric is the Newtonian potential $\Phi$, related by $\Phi/c^{2} \sim v^{2}/c^{2} \sim \epsilon^{2}$, which guarantees that the system is bounded by its own gravity.

The Newtonian limit cannot be uniform everywhere for all time because any compact binary system will eventually spiral together due to backreaction from the emission of gravitational waves, causing higher order effects to dominate the lowest order Newtonian dynamics.
Divergent integrals in the post-Newtonian approximation may be avoided by carefully defining the Newtonian limit.
The use of the Newtonian limit provides a strong indication that the post-Newtonian hierarchy is an asymptotic approximation to general relativity.

The discovery of the binary neutron star system PSR 1913+16 was a strong reason to have renewed interest in the post-Newtonian approximation, as it is the first system found in which general relativistic gravity plays a fundamental role in its evolution.
The effect of radiation reaction appears in the form of a potential force at the order of $\epsilon^5$ higher than the Newtonian force in the equations of motion.
Coalescing binary neutron stars are the most promising candidates of sources of gravitational waves for kilometer-size interferometric gravitational wave detectors.
The waveform from coalescing binaries can be predicted with high accuracy compared to other sources.
To make a meaningful comparison between theory and observation, detailed waveforms generated by the motion up to 4 PN order (order $\epsilon^8$ higher than Newtonian) are required.
The 3.5 PN waveform includes tail terms which manifest nonlinearity of general relativity.
The dominant part of the tail term originates from the phase shift of the wave due to the Coulomb part of the gravitational field.
The 3 PN ADM Hamiltonian in ADMTT gauge derived by Jaranowski and Schäfer contains an undetermined coefficient $\omega_{\mathrm{kinetic}}$ due to regularization issues.
The 3 PN equations of motion derived by Blanchet and Faye contain one undetermined coefficient $\lambda$.
The present authors' derivation of 3 PN equations of motion for relativistic compact binaries does not use Dirac delta distributions and finds no undetermined coefficients.

At least up to 3 PN order, a particle (with a strong internal gravity) follows a regularized (in some sense) geodesic equation in a dynamical spacetime, a part of whose gravitational field the particle itself generates.
The resulting 3 PN equations of motion respect Lorentz invariance, admit a conserved energy (modulo the 2.5 PN radiation reaction effect), and are free from any ambiguity.
A particle with strong internal gravity moves on a geodesic of some smooth metric part which is produced by the particle itself.
The Newtonian equations involve six variables: density, pressure, gravitational potential, and velocity.
The magnitude of the gravitational potential is of order $\epsilon^{2}$ due to the balance between gravity and the centrifugal force.
The scaling of the time variable expresses that weaker gravity corresponds to a longer time scale.
The Einstein equations are nonlinear in field variables, preventing the enforcement of Newtonian scaling everywhere in spacetime.
The choice of vanishing free data for the field corresponds to the absence of radiation far away from the source.
The limit $\epsilon \to 0$ along the defined integral curve is not unique and is defined by a smooth nowhere vanishing vector field on the fiber bundle.
The map defining the Newtonian limit never reaches the fiber $\epsilon=0$ (Minkowski spacetime), implying there is no pure vacuum Newtonian limit.
A simple post-Newtonian iteration is meaningful only in the near zone and is not useful outside of the near zone (far zone) where wave effects are manifest.
The characteristics are determined by the operator $(\eta^{\alpha\beta}-h^{\alpha\beta})\partial_{\alpha}\partial_{\beta}$, and thus the light cone deviates from that in the flat spacetime.
In the study of the gravitational field near the source it is not necessary to consider the deviation of the light cone from the flat one.
The homogeneous solutions play no important role.
The domain of integral is finite as long as $\epsilon \neq 0$ and their diameter increases like $\epsilon^{-1}$ as $\epsilon \to 0$.

findings.claim: The precession motion is a consequence of the $\beta$ motion, which perturbs back the $\alpha$ motion.
The precession motion $\omega_{\alpha}^{(\text{precession})}$ is not caused by nonlinear translational motion, as the translation frequencies do not change with pressure.
The precession motion arises due to the fast spinning $\alpha$ degree of freedom, as well as, the nutation motion of $\beta$.
Precession motion is a degree of freedom that could be utilised for torque sensing with the sensitivities to resolve single electron and even nuclear spins at low pressure.

The precession motion can be used for dynamical model selection to distinguish between quantum and classical evolution due to the inherent nonlinearities in rotation motion, if sufficient coherence can be prepared.
The dynamics of a non-spherical levitated nanoparticle in vacuum includes light torque-induced precession and nutation in addition to translation and rotation.
The theoretical model's numerical simulations and approximate expressions for motional frequencies are in good agreement with experiments.

The scattering torque drives the system into a fast spinning motion, while the gradient torque aligns the system with the polarization to minimize electric dipole potential energy, resulting in nutation and precession.
The particle starts to spin until an asymptotic rotational frequency is reached, which is constrained by friction due to gas collisions.

Once the nanoparticle starts to spin, it is unable to fully align, but rather settles around an equilibrium position $\beta_{0} \neq \frac{\pi}{2}$, which can be understood in terms of angular momenta addition.

Any small perturbation, e.g. gas collisions, will make the $\beta$ angle oscillate around the $\beta_{0}$ angle, which results in libration (nutation) motion with frequency $\omega_{\beta}^{(\text{mutation})}$.

The coupling between $\beta$ and $\alpha$ creates a second frequency for the $\alpha$ motion, denoted by $\omega_{\alpha}^{(\text{precession})}$, which can be visualized as a slow precession of the $z''$ axis about the z axis.
$\omega_{\alpha}^{(\mathrm{spin})}$ and $\omega_{\beta}^{(\mathrm{nutation})}$ scale linearly with the laser power P, and are inversely proportional to the gas pressure p.
Translation frequencies do not show pressure dependency but scale proportionately to the square root of laser power P.
The x and y translation peaks are separated due to the use of elliptically polarized light which generates an asymmetric optical trap after reflection from the paraboloidal mirror.

The rotational frequency $\omega_{\gamma}^{(\mathrm{spin})}$ changes with the damping, $\Gamma_{c}$, which depends linearly on the gas pressure, p, i.e. $\omega_{\gamma}^{(\mathrm{spin})} \propto \frac{1}{\Gamma_{c}} \propto \frac{1}{p}$.
The frequency of $\omega_{\gamma}^{(\mathrm{spin})}$ has a dependency on the laser power P in agreement with the dependency on the photon scattering torque, $N_{s} \propto P$.
Light-matter interactions introduce couplings between translation and rotation, which explain the observed sidebands and higher harmonics.
The precession frequency $\omega_{\alpha}^{(\text{precession})}$ has a weak dependence on the laser power P, i.e. $\omega_{\alpha}^{(\text{precession})} = \Delta\omega|_{P_{0}}$.
The $\beta$ libration is due to the coupling between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ motion.
The simulated dominant frequencies are in perfect agreement with experimental data.
The approximate expressions in Eqs. (B3) - (B5) show good agreement within order of magnitude with simulation parameters.
Eqs. (B3) - (B5) can be used for estimating the initial simulation parameters for the fitting algorithm.
The expressions for variance of momentum (angular momentum) fluctuations are good estimates for a system that is not highly anisotropic.
For highly anisotropic objects, the moment of inertia and electric susceptibility tensors have to be taken into account.
The analysis reproduces the transition to the photon recoil heating regime for translations in accordance with Fig. 3 from [20].
